newsitem.title: USA: Sumitomo Chemical sues Dow in patent dispute.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Chemical sues Dow in patent dispute.

text.p: Sumitomo Chemical Co, Inabata & Co Ltd's American unit and Summit Specialty Corp have sued Dow Chemical Co in a dispute over three Dow patents for making low-chloride epoxy resins.
In papers filed this month in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, the plaintiffs claim the Dow patents are invalid.

They also assert a legal right to import resins into the United States without being liable for infringement because "the resin was already in substantial and continuous sale" by their predecessors prior to 1988.
In September, Dow sued the plaintiffs in the U.S. District Court of eastern Michigan for infringement of the three patents described in court papers as the '255, '863 and '061 patents.
Sumitomo, of Tokyo, Japan, manufactures epoxy resin, which is imported and sold in the U.S. by Inabat and Summit.
The lawsuit also seeks a court ruling the plaintiffs not be held liable for any damages that may be awarded for alleged infringement "prior to the receipt of statutory notice of infringement."
